chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: May we combine al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' while resident, before the twilight disappears, without any excuse? He said: There is no harm.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that those among them which are restricted by the permissibility of combining the two without any excuse and without any justification are to be understood as a kind of concession and permissibility, even though what we have presented earlier is more excellent and preferable. And those among them that are free of that qualification are to be understood as referring to the state of travel and other excuses. And that which indicates the permissibility of that in the state of travel and the state of necessity...

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةِ: a concession granted in the law
key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight whose disappearance marks a later phase of time
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: the state of residence, as opposed to travel
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: a legal excuse or justifying reason

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' before the twilight disappears without an excuse?
ai.summary: This hadith states that combining al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' before the disappearance of twilight while resident and without an excuse is permissible. The accompanying scholarly note explains that such reports indicate a concession, while the more preferable practice is separation, and that other reports are understood in relation to travel or necessity.
